back: Knowledge and understanding about a market, its consumers and companies, generated through observing behaviour. They unlock opportunities by (1) understanding behaviour and its drivers, (2) tracking changing needs, (3) understanding group perceptions.
Looking back (historical data) – present/real time (Voice of Customer, NPS) – looking forward (trend forecasting, statistical modelling).
Primary: collected for a specific purpose (experimental/non-experimental, qualitative/quantitative). Secondary: already compiled, internal or external, more time- and cost-effective.
1 problem/question · 2 sources & research design · 3 data collection method · 4 data collection · 5 analysis & interpretation.
Industry description & outlook · target market · competitive analysis · distribution channels · barriers to entry · regulation (compliance costs).
Euromonitor (GMID): market analyses, consumers, countries, companies. LS:N Global: consumer behaviour & trends. Statista: statistics portal. Xerfi: industry studies (France/international).
A new manifestation among people – in behaviour, attitude or expectation – of a fundamental human need, want or desire (Mason et al., 2015).
Macro: ≥ 5 years, many industries (maker movement, wellness boom). Micro: early influencers → mass adoption in 1–2 years; smaller realisations of macro trends.
Basic needs (rarely changing) + drivers of change (no trend without change) + innovations (examples of how a trend exists, not trends themselves).

front: Weak signal / cultural brailling / horizon scanning
back: Weak signal: overlooked anomaly, meaningful in clusters. Cultural brailling (Faith Popcorn): sensing change daily. Horizon scanning: structured scan of the STEEPLE landscape.
Review previous trends · research future known events · establish and describe the current situation · analyse unexpected events · identify common threads.
Trend maturity (how do expectations play out now?), locality (in my target market?), industry (in my industry?) – Mattin et al., 2015.
Inspirations · basic needs · drivers of change (shifts + triggers) · emerging consumer expectations.
Innovation potential (vision, business model, product/service/experience, marketing) · Who (new customer groups, personas).

Shifts: long-term macro changes (aging society, rich–poor divide, climate challenge, people on the move, urban transition, emerging middle class). Triggers: immediate changes (technologies, political/social events, economic shocks, environmental incidents).
